nodes.name: Big bluestem
nodes.desc: A tall warm-season grass that dominates the preserve grasslands alongside switchgrass, reaching 6 to 8 feet by September.

nodes.name: Switchgrass
nodes.desc: A tall native bunchgrass that grows with big bluestem and helps make up the dense tallgrass cover.

nodes.name: Milkweeds
nodes.desc: Prairie wildflowers whose leaves feed monarch caterpillars and whose flowers feed many insects. Antelope-horns and butterfly milkweed are well recorded here.

nodes.name: American bison
nodes.desc: Free-ranging herd of roughly 2,500 animals used since 1989 to restore the prairie. Grazing and patch burning together shape the habitat.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Common in the wooded parts of the preserve. Eats leaves, forbs and grasses and is prey for coyotes and bobcats.

nodes.name: Prairie vole
nodes.desc: A small grass-eating rodent and the most recorded mammal near the preserve. Hawks, harriers and coyotes all take voles.

nodes.name: Hispid cotton rat
nodes.desc: A common grassland rodent that eats plants and is food for hawks, harriers and coyotes.

nodes.name: Eastern cottontail
nodes.desc: Eats grasses and wildflowers including milkweed and is prey for hawks, coyotes and bobcats.

nodes.name: Two-striped grasshopper
nodes.desc: A large grasshopper that chews grasses and forbs and feeds birds such as prairie-chickens.

nodes.name: Monarch butterfly
nodes.desc: Caterpillars feed on milkweed; adults sip nectar from prairie flowers. The preserve names monarchs among its highlights.

nodes.name: Greater prairie-chicken
nodes.desc: A threatened grouse that eats seeds, green plants and insects such as grasshoppers. Males boom on open display grounds each spring.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A widespread hawk that hunts rodents and rabbits over open ground. Recorded in GloBI taking voles and cotton rats.

nodes.name: Northern harrier
nodes.desc: A low-flying hawk of open grassland, common on the preserve in fall and winter, hunting small rodents.

nodes.name: Dickcissel
nodes.desc: A grassland songbird named among the preserve highlights. Feeds on insects including grasshoppers during the breeding season.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Soars over the prairie and cleans up carcasses of animals such as deer and rabbits.

nodes.name: American burying beetle
nodes.desc: An endangered beetle present here in summer. Adults need small carcasses to breed and bury them to feed their young.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A top predator of the preserve. GloBI records it eating voles, cotton rats, rabbits and deer.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A secretive wild cat named among the preserve highlights. Hunts rabbits, rodents and sometimes deer.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm-season grasses grow fastest in summer heat and long days.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Spring and early summer rain sets how tall the grass grows.

nodes.name: Patch-burn fire
nodes.desc: The preserve burns roughly a third of the prairie each year. Fire keeps brush out and draws bison to fresh regrowth.

nodes.name: Prairie soil
nodes.desc: Deep root systems build rich soil and store nutrients under the grass.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down dead grass, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
